      Problem: Location: lines 84–88; Issue: Truncation should remove only the incomplete trailing line/character, not the first line of output.; Suggested minimal fix: Replace the rev/cut pipeline with a bash-only approach that preserves all complete lines:; max_bytes_actual=$((max_bytes * 4)); if [ "${raw_bytes}" -gt "${max_bytes_actual}" ]; then; truncated=$(head -c "${max_bytes_actual}" "${tmp_out}"); if [[ "$truncated" == *$'\n'* ]]; then; printf '%s' "${truncated%$'\n'*}" > "${CONSOLIDATOR_RAW_FILE}"; : > "${CONSOLIDATOR_RAW_FILE}"; printf '\n... [TRUNCATED_BY_OUTPUT_CAP] ...\n' >> "${CONSOLIDATOR_RAW_FILE}"; capped=1; This keeps all lines ending with a newline (complete lines) and drops only the final partial line, without reordering or dropping the first line. It also remains UTF-8 safe because it works with raw bytes and does not split multi-byte characters within kept lines.; Estimated lines changed: ~8; HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 5
